knowledge_misuse: KR-PCB-005 is presented as 'decisive' against Option C ('a separate driver card is justified only if it mates directly at the gate/Kelvin pins'); the rule's statement only prescribes how a plug-in driver must mate and its applicability explicitly includes plug-in drivers. The rejection of C should rest on the rule's rationale (connector inductance), the SKILL-002 scope note and cost/assembly, not on the rule as a criterion.

KR-GD-008's exclusion is worded for 'short on-board links'; extending it to a board-to-board connector is an adaptation that both the assumptions agent (A-21 conditional) and the gate-driver agent explicitly made conditional on a single board, requiring CB-GD-003 RS-422 otherwise. The architecture resolved this conflict silently instead of preserving it (TIDA-010054's single-ended SN74LVC126A control-card practice would be the supporting evidence).

KR-TH-001 (hard constraint, owned by the thermal agent) was used as a sanity check with inputs that contradict the owning agents (R_pad 0.5 K/W vs 0.80; P_device from the 400 V corner with P_total from the 440 V corner), yielding an optimistic 'acceptable' R_th range up to 1.1 K/W; the thermal agent's table (<= 0.98 K/W at max R for 150 degC) should be referenced instead.

KR-ISO-001 is applied only to the HV/SELV barrier; its second clause (barrier between independently referenced driver channels, HS/LS islands) is not carried into pcb_constraints although the gate-driver agent lists three barriers.

The SKILL-002 '~200 kW+' sentence is a scope note under 'Not applicable / out of scope' about busbar systems and appears only in the skill (not in the CGD1700HB2M-UNA analysis); citing it as a reason to reject C is acceptable as supporting evidence but should not be labelled as a rule.
No reference instance values were copied (TIDA 300 x 180 mm and CGD island/card sizes used as benchmarks only) - no misuse found there.

summary: The Option B recommendation (power PCB with drivers, bias modules and sensing isolators plus a stacked SELV control PCB over a 2 x 25 mezzanine) is confirmed: every area, height, volume, cost-index, scoring, air-gap and current figure recomputes from the stated inputs, the V1 15 % utilisation precedent is reproduced from placement.json (14.4 %), and B leads under every weighting I could re-run. Corrections are needed because (1) the HV area is 33,600 mm2 at 73 % utilisation, not 28,800 mm2 at 86 %; (2) the heat-sink envelope, fan concept and inductor/film spacing contradict the thermal agent's already-selected Fischer LAM 5 K 100 12 with integrated fan (185 x 60 mm strip, 55 mm high; 20 mm spacings), which makes the 230 x 170 mm stretch outline unlikely and adds an unbudgeted 0.5 A fan path through the mezzanine and the 1.425 A eFuse limit; (3) the single-ended mezzanine signalling silently overrides the assumptions agent's A-21 condition and the gate-driver agent's RS-422 requirement for separated boards; (4) the stack-up thickness does not add up (1.78 mm vs 2.0 mm); (5) the KR-TH-001 sanity check mixes loss corners and uses a 0.5 K/W pad where the thermal agent has 0.80 K/W, so 1.1 K/W is not acceptable (T_J up to 157 degC at max R); and (6) KR-PCB-005 is over-read as a rejection criterion for Option C. The 11 mm Samtec stack height remains unverified (Samtec documents inaccessible in this run). None of these changes alters the choice of Option B.
